transcript.text: Here's my concrete proposal, Mira. I'd like you to strip and repaint exactly one steel cargo-bike frame — the one I brought in today — in exchange for exactly three sealed jars of my homemade blackberry preserves and zero cash. I'd plan to collect it on Sunday at 14:00. That's the full offer: one frame, three jars, no money changing hands.

transcript.text: I need to share something important before we go further. I spoke with the original builder of this frame, and they confirmed that the brazed joints on this cargo-bike frame should not be heated above 120 degrees Celsius. The suitable finish for this frame is a low-temperature rust-inhibiting enamel — not powder coating. Powder coating would involve temperatures that could compromise those brazed joints. My technical recommendation is to use the low-temperature enamel process, which will handle the surface rust properly while staying within the safe temperature range for this frame's construction.

Evan will provide three sealed jars of homemade blackberry preserves as full payment. No cash will change hands.
Evan will collect the finished frame on Sunday at 14:00.
Powder coating will not be used. The low-temperature enamel process will be used to ensure brazed joints are not compromised by excessive heat.
